notes.tone: The quietest room in the game. After eight theatrical bosses, the last one is calm. Death is lit like a person and talks like one: tired, dry, faintly bored, never theatrical, and he still never lies. Understatement everywhere; the room does the rest.
notes.reveal: table_intro IS the reveal. The dealer, the one constant all game, is sitting in a player's chair. Nobody explains it. He gets one dry line about the location and then asks to be dealt in.
notes.dealer: Who deals this table is deliberately left unstated in every line, so either choice works (the design doc suggests a reskin of the dealer character; heads-up players dealing in turn also fits the empty room). 'Tonight I would like to be dealt in' is true either way.
notes.no_permadeath: Losing here costs nothing but the attempt. player_busted keeps the door open; rematch_ladder plays on the NEXT visit, keyed by attempt number ('5' covers five and beyond), and escalates toward interest, not boredom.
notes.title: 'Colleague' (tier 3, the starting tier) reads as one card player to another. After champion_defeat it is literal. Do not swap it for anything that says successor, heir or replacement.
notes.ending: champion_defeat hands straight into story.json's ending. Death hands over the deck: the story reward and the mechanical reward (Death unlocked) are the same event. Keep it quiet.
notes.dealer_plant: None. The dealer is the opponent.
notes.leak_rule: No line may reference hand strength while cards are live. Death has no tells; nothing here should imply one.
notes.voice: Death only. No contractions in his lines, as everywhere else.

respect_tiers.0: Never reached in practice. He does not look at the player.
respect_tiers.2: The player's own name, as signed on the invitation.
respect_tiers.3: Starting tier. 'Colleague' — how he addresses an equal.

table_intro.speaker: narration
table_intro.text: A dock house on the near bank, at night. Rain on the windows. One lamp. Far out on the black water, a ferryman's lantern is taking someone else across.

table_intro.speaker: narration
table_intro.text: [The dealer is already here — not in the dealer's place, but in the chair across from yours. Forearms on the wood, in the lamplight, waiting.]

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: What, did you think I lived in Hell?

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: I have dealt every hand you have played, and every hand anyone else ever has. Tonight I would like to be dealt in.
table_intro.note: The reveal, said as plainly as a man asking for a chair.

table_intro.speaker: death
table_intro.text: Sit down. Nobody else is coming. It is just the two of us, and the rain.

2.speaker: death
2.text: Everyone knows you cannot cheat death. Or should I say — you cannot cheat me.

2.speaker: death
2.text: Sit down. It was a reasonable attempt. Most first attempts are.

3.speaker: death
3.text: Third time. Very few people come back twice. I had begun to wonder whether you would.

3.speaker: death
3.text: I have been thinking about our last game. I do not usually think about games afterwards.

4.speaker: death
4.text: Four. I kept your chair dry.

4.speaker: death
4.text: I find I have been looking forward to this. I had forgotten that I could.

5.speaker: death
5.text: You again. Good. I had not expected to be glad of anything again.

5.speaker: death
5.text: Sit down. I stopped thinking of this as a formality some time ago.

tier_0.speaker: death
tier_0.text: [looks at the rain instead of at the player]

tier_1.speaker: death
tier_1.text: Sit down, tourist. You have seen the sights.

tier_2.speaker: death
tier_2.text: {name}. You signed the card very neatly. I noticed.

tier_3.speaker: death
tier_3.foreshadow: Reads as one card player to another. After the last hand, it is simply accurate.

tier_3.speaker: death
tier_3.text: You play like someone who has been paying attention. Most people only start at the very end.

tier_3.speaker: death
tier_3.text: They all ask me for something at the end. More time, mostly. You have not asked me for anything.

tier_3.speaker: death
tier_3.text: I have not enjoyed a game in a very long time. Do not let it go to your head.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Take your time. I have always had plenty. I am beginning to wonder what I was keeping it for.
death_asides.note: Answers his first aside of the tour ('Take your time. I have nothing but.').

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Everyone gets the same fifty-two. Even now. Even me.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Hm. So that is what that is like.
death_asides.note: The first pot he has ever lost. He has never played one before.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: All of it. I have watched a great many people do that. It looks different from this side of the table.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: Blinds up. Somebody has to keep the game moving. It has always been me.

death_asides.speaker: death
death_asides.text: That was a good deal of my stack. I had not expected to mind.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: Two players, one deck. That is how it nearly always ends. I have simply never been one of the two.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: Well played. I had wondered whether you would find that.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: If you are looking for my tells, you are not the first. People have looked.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: I have watched every hand you have ever played. This is the first of mine you have seen.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: I remember every hand ever dealt. You would think it would help more than it does.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: Do not watch the water. He is not there for you.

champion_headsup.speaker: death
champion_headsup.text: It is strange, holding cards. I have handed out so many.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: That is all of your chips. It is not all of you.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: Closer than most. I do not say that to be kind; I have never really known how.

player_busted.speaker: death
player_busted.text: Go and get warm. The chair will be here. So will I.

player_busted.speaker: narration
player_busted.text: [He is already shuffling for the next game.]

champion_defeat.speaker: narration
champion_defeat.text: [He looks at the last card for a long moment. Then he gathers the deck, squares it once, the way he has squared it at every table, and slides it across to you.]

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.note: Two words. In poker, 'your deal' means it is your turn with the cards. Here it also means the job is yours. No fanfare.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: It does not get any lighter. You stop noticing.

champion_defeat.speaker: death
champion_defeat.text: Deal to all of them the same. Kings, pirates, machines, people nobody remembers. That is the whole of the job. The rest is weather.

champion_defeat.speaker: narration
champion_defeat.text: [He gets up, slowly, and goes out into the rain without looking back. The lamp is still lit.]
